title: Should You Hire a Lawyer After a Washington Crash?
metaDescription: Should you hire a lawyer after a Washington accident? District of Columbia fault rules, injury severity, and free matching options.
excerpt: Educational Washington, DC guide — 3-year SOL, local hospitals, and insurer tactics. Not legal advice.

sections.heading: Signs you may need counsel
paragraphs: Hospitalization, surgery, disputed fault, denied coverage, or lowball offers after Washington crashes are common triggers for attorney consultation.

sections.heading: How District of Columbia contingency fees typically work
paragraphs: Most personal injury attorneys work on contingency — you pay no upfront fee; they receive a percentage of recovery if successful. Verify terms in writing.

sections.heading: What an attorney handles
paragraphs: Evidence preservation, lien negotiation, insurer correspondence, and litigation if settlement fails.

sections.heading: WreckMatch's role
paragraphs: We match Washington residents with independent District of Columbia attorneys. We are not a law firm and do not provide legal advice.

faq.question: Is this legal advice for my Washington case?
faq.answer: No. This is general education from WreckMatch LLC, a referral service — not a law firm. Consult a licensed attorney for advice about your situation.

faq.question: What is the statute of limitations in District of Columbia?
faq.answer: Most injury claims face a 3-year deadline, but exceptions apply. Verify your dates with counsel.
